Article Title: NSE IPO: Stock lists at Rs 1,800 versus issue price of Rs 1,785 on BSE with 0.8% premium; check details
Article Text:
Before the IPO opened for subscription, NSE had raised Rs 6,746 crore from more than 150 anchor investors.

NSE Debuts on BSE, MSEI

NSE IPO GMP

NSE IPO listing date today: National Stock Exchange of India ’s shares debuted on the Bombay Stock Exchange at Rs 1,800 versus an issue price of Rs 1,785, marking a premium of around 0.8%.NSE made its stock market debut with a market capitalisation of more than Rs 4.45 lakh crore, becoming the second listed stock exchange in India. Its valuation at listing was significantly higher than that of rival BSE, whose current market capitalisation stands at Rs 1.33 lakh crore.Market participants were tracking grey market movements closely ahead of the listing, which is among the most anticipated market debuts of the year so far. Analysts said restrictions on exits by most large shareholders could limit the availability of NSE shares in the near term, potentially putting upward pressure on prices at a later stage.NSE's market debut gives investors an opportunity to assess how the exchange should be valued. Its longer-term growth outlook helped attract strong institutional interest, while retail investors appeared more cautious amid concerns about derivatives volumes, regulatory pressures and the possibility of more shares entering the market.Although investors remain broadly positive on NSE's longer-term prospects, the stock's performance in the months following its listing could depend on the amount of additional equity that becomes available once the lock-in periods for existing shareholders come to an end.In a circular issued on Wednesday, MSE said NSE's equity shares would be admitted for trading on its capital market segment under the ‘Permitted to trade’ category, effective September 24.The Metropolitan Stock Exchange is a Sebi-recognised national stock exchange that operates an electronic trading platform covering capital markets, equity derivatives, currency derivatives and debt segments. Its platform includes equity and index derivatives, debt and currency derivatives, with more than 250 listings and over 3,100 companies available for trading.The development comes days after NSE MD and CEO Ashish Chauhan made it clear that the exchange would not approach Sebi for permission to trade its own shares on its platform. Existing regulations of the market regulator do not permit a recognised stock exchange to list its own securities on its own trading platform.In the unlisted market, traders saw a grey market premium or GMP of around 2.2%. The stock has listed on a waek note with less than 1% premium over its issue price.The GMP was much higher earlier at Rs 250-310 a share, or roughly 14-17%. The steep decline had suggested expectations of only modest gains when the shares list."While investors have been waiting for the NSE listing for long, the enthusiasm has moderated because of the large issue size and expected supply," Abhay Doshi, co-founder of UnlistedArena.com told ET.At the IPO's upper price of Rs 1,785 per share, NSE's valuation stands at Rs 4.42 lakh crore, compared with Rs 1.33 lakh crore for rival BSE. Some market participants said the balance between available supply and investor demand could play an important role in determining how NSE shares perform in the initial trading sessions after listing.The listing brings to an end NSE's long-running journey towards becoming a listed company and make it India's second listed stock exchange after BSE.NSE launched its initial public offering earlier this month, seeking to raise Rs 22,562 crore through a 12.64 crore-share offer for sale (OFS) by existing shareholders.Since the issue was entirely an OFS, NSE itself will not receive any money from the IPO. The proceeds will instead accrue to the shareholders selling their stakes through the offering.The IPO price band was fixed at Rs 1,700 to Rs 1,785 per share. With the lot size set at 8 shares, retail investors were required to invest a minimum of Rs 14,280 to apply for the issue.Before the IPO opened for subscription, NSE had raised Rs 6,746 crore from more than 150 anchor investors.Foreign portfolio investors made up Rs 2,883 crore, or 43%, of the total anchor book. The anchor round saw participation from more than 20 foreign long-only funds, including Singapore sovereign wealth fund GIC, Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and Norges Bank.Domestic institutional participation was similarly spread across investors. More than 25 mutual funds, along with 11 insurance and pension companies, invested around Rs 3,588 crore, accounting for 53% of the anchor book.LIC, which is NSE's largest shareholder with a 10.72% stake, also participated in the anchor round. LIC, LIC Mutual Fund and LIC Pension Fund together invested more than Rs 500 crore. The investment was made even though LIC's existing shareholding in NSE is larger than the stake being offered through the IPO.The SBI group also took part in the anchor book through SBI Mutual Fund, SBI General, SBI Life and SBI Pension Fund. State Bank of India and SBI Capital Markets are together selling a 1% stake in NSE, while the group's combined investment in the exchange through its various entities exceeds Rs 400 crore.NSE's first public issue attracted strong demand during the three-day subscription period from September 17 to September 21. The IPO was subscribed nearly six times the shares on offer. Qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) drove the demand, subscribing to their reserved portion around 13 times, while the portions allocated to retail investors and non-institutional investors (NII) were subscribed 1.4 times and 6.6 times, respectively.
Article Summary: Nse made its stock market debut with a market capitalisation of more than rs 4.45 lakh crore, becoming the second listed stock exchange in india. Its valuation at listing was significantly higher than that of rival bse, whose current market cap stands at rs 1.33 lakh crore.

Article Title: Private retailers start rationing diesel sales
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Private fuel retailers have started rationing diesel sales at their outlets amid a surge in global crude prices, driven by supply constraints caused by the ongoing West Asia conflict. However, state-owned oil marketing companies Indian Oil, HPCL and BPCL confirmed there was no such restriction at their outlets.The impact is limited, as the three public sector oil companies operate around 90% of the more than one lakh fuel stations in the country.Several Jio-BP retail outlets TOI spoke to confirmed they had been directed to sell only 50 litres of diesel per customer. Daily diesel sales have also been capped at 6,000 litres.Retailers operating Russian oil major Rosneft-backed Nayara Energy outlets said the cap ranged from 70 to 200 litres per transaction. The restrictions are likely to affect long-haul commercial vehicles with larger fuel tanks, particularly in remote areas with fewer fuel stations.
Article Summary: Private fuel retailers have started rationing diesel sales at their outlets. The impact is limited, as the three public sector oil companies operate around 90% of the more than one lakh fuel stations in the country. The restrictions are likely to affect long-haul commercial vehicles with larger fuel tanks, particularly in remote areas.

Article Title: Banks role must shift from supporting economy to financing transformation: Setty
Article Text:
SBI chairman C S Setty said at the SBI Banking and Economics Conclave in Mumbai on Wednesday.

MUMBAI: India’s financial system will need to evolve to finance the country’s next phase of economic expansion, with banks playing a larger role in supporting higher-value manufacturing, new technologies, the green transition and enterprises seeking to compete globally, SBI chairman C S Setty said at the SBI Banking and Economics Conclave in Mumbai on Wednesday.“The banking and financial system will need to evolve alongside it, providing the financial architecture that enables innovation, investment, and strength,” Setty said, referring to India’s transition towards becoming a leading economic force.Setty said India’s resilience through successive global and domestic headwinds had strengthened the financial system’s ability to participate in the next stage of economic expansion. But sustaining that momentum would require improvements in productivity and competitiveness, deeper integration with global value chains and the emergence of enterprises capable of competing at scale in international markets.“The question is not simply how fast we grow, but how effectively we convert growth into global informativeness and leadership,” he said.Setty pointed to India’s large and dynamic domestic market, young workforce, improving infrastructure, domestic capital and globally competitive services sector as strengths that could support the next phase of growth.Digital public infrastructure, he said, had demonstrated how technology, scale and public purpose could come together to create solutions with relevance beyond India.The next wave of global investment is likely to be shaped by sunrise sectors such as renewables, semiconductors, energy storage and green hydrogen, as well as robotics, biotechnology and frontier technologies, Setty said. India has the talent, entrepreneurial energy and technological capabilities to participate meaningfully in these sectors, he said.“The larger opportunity lies in translating these trends into businesses, technologies, manufacturing capabilities, and intellectual property that can command a global footprint,” Setty said.This transition will require the financial sector to support innovation and investment as the economy moves towards higher-value manufacturing and globally competitive enterprises. The banking sector, he said, would have a significant role in enhancing infrastructure, enterprise and innovation as part of the broader transformation of the productive economy.The conclave brings together policymakers, regulators, industry leaders and economists to examine how India can sustain its economic momentum, deepen confidence and create conditions for the next generation of Indian enterprises and institutions to build a global presence. Setty said the discussions should result not just in fresh perspectives but in ideas that could contribute to the country's next phase of development.
Article Summary: Sbi chairman c s setty said at the sbi banking and economics conclave in mumbai on wednesday. Setty: india’s resilience through successive global and domestic headwinds had strengthened the financial system. The banking sector would have a significant role in enhancing infrastructure, enterprise and innovation, he said.

It marks the beginning of a new academic environment where knowledge, technology, research and human values come together.The inauguration of the Ramaiah Institute of Science and Management and the foundation laying of Nareyana Pragnalaya – ‘Abode of Wisdom’, mark a significant milestone in the continuing educational journey of the Ramaiah Group of Institutions and Gokula Education Foundation.Building on a legacy of contributing to India’s knowledge society, the new initiatives reflect a vision of education that brings together global academic collaboration, emerging technologies, research and innovation, while remaining rooted in the values of wisdom, character and social responsibility. Article Title: Nitin Gadkari says India is sending Rs 22 lakh crore out of country to import petrol, diesel, and gas; pushes sugar mills to make compressed bio gas, bio-manure, and sustainable aviation fuel
Article Text:
According to Gadkari, making better use of sugarcane by-products could also improve returns for farmers. (Image for representative purpose only)

Make gas, ethanol, aviation fuel

Barrier free tolling to save fuel and costs

India imports most of the fuel it consumes - be it crude oil, LPG, or even LNG. Union Minister for Road Transport and Highways Nitin Gadkari has said that India’s agriculture sector can help drive down imported costs of fossil fuels, while at the same time using a combination of futuristic technology and a forward-looking vision if it is to become economically sustainable and help drive prosperity in rural India.Addressing the National Efficiency Awards ceremony organised by the National Federation of Cooperative Sugar Factories, Gadkari recently said producing sugar alone is no longer economically sustainable in view of global market conditions and the higher cost of production in India.Gadkari has called on sugar mills to expand into value-added by-products, particularly compressed bio-gas (CBG), ethanol, bio-manure and sustainable aviation fuel."Instead of dumping waste into road embankments, if we convert it into gas - into CBG - our imports will decline. Understand this figure: Rs 22 lakh crore. We are sending Rs 22 lakh crore out of our country to import fossil fuels - petrol, diesel, and gas," Gadkari said according to ANI.He pointed out that India's sugar output is between 300 and 350 lakh tonnes, while domestic consumption ranges from 280 to 300 lakh tonnes.The resulting surplus has put pressure on sugar prices.At the same time, he said, countries such as Brazil have a significantly lower production cost, at Rs 23 per kg compared with India's Rs 33 to Rs 34 per kg."The future of plain sugar is mediocre at best. I won't mince words: diversifying into complementary by-products guarantees a strong future," the Minister said.According to Gadkari, making better use of sugarcane by-products could also improve returns for farmers. He said the additional value generated through these products could eventually enable sugar mills to pay farmers as much as Rs 6,000 per tonne of sugarcane, compared with the current Rs 4,000.Gadkari also underlined the scale of India's agricultural waste and its potential as a source of bio-energy.Punjab and Haryana alone generate around 220 lakh tonnes of paddy stubble, he said. Five tonnes of stubble can produce one tonne of CBG, which he described as a way to address stubble burning and air pollution while simultaneously creating wealth in rural areas."Technology has arrived, allowing us to produce CBG from stubble, bamboo, rice straw, bagasse, and Napier grass. The Government of India launched a dedicated scheme. Look at the numbers: 1,908 CBG plants have been registered across the country, with 132 already operational," he said.India has the potential to produce 50,000 tonnes of CBG per day, Gadkari said, but present output accounts for only around two per cent of that capacity.The government has also introduced mandatory procurement obligations along with a fixed procurement price of Rs 106 per kg. He said the initiative could bring Rs 2.5 lakh crore into the rural economy and create as many as 15 lakh jobs.The Minister further called on the sugar industry to make greater use of artificial intelligence, precision farming and agricultural drones to reduce the cost of inputs and improve farm productivity.He cited the decision to permit ethanol production directly from corn as an example, saying the move had resulted in Rs 45,000 crore being transferred directly to farmers in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.Meanwhile, India is moving to a FASTag-enabled barrier-free tolling system which will not only save time, but also fuel costs.The government could gain an annual benefit of as much as Rs 25,000 crore once the electronic toll collection system FASTag is fully implemented, Gadkari said recently.Gadkari said the government is targeting the removal of barriers from all toll plazas on national highways by March 2027 as part of its plan to make toll collection completely barrier-free."When the system will go fully live, then our department alone would deliver a benefit of Rs 20,000-25,000 crore per year to the Government of India because of the use of FASTags," Gadkari said at the Global Fintech Fest.The minister said FASTag adoption has already resulted in a 10% increase in toll collections, translating into an additional Rs 7,000 crore approximately. Total revenue generated at toll booths has consequently risen to more than Rs 82,000 crore, according to Gadkari.
Article Summary: India imports most of the fuel it consumes - be it crude oil, lpg, or even lng. Nitin gadkari has called on sugar mills to expand into value-added by-products, particularly compressed bio-gas (cbg), ethanol, bio-manure and sustainable aviation fuel.

Article Title: New Jersey inspectors found 62 large natural-gas generators running without required permits at a massive AI data center; the state has now imposed a record $1.07 million penalty
Article Text:
Representative image

What the inspection uncovered

Why the permits were required

The record $1.07 million penalty

DataOne’s response

A major AI infrastructure project

Concerns from nearby residents

Why the power system matters

The planned shift to fuel cells

A test for New Jersey’s data-center policy

What happens next

New Jersey has imposed a record $1.07 million penalty on DataOne after inspectors found 62 large natural-gas generators installed and operating without required air-pollution permits at the company’s massive artificial intelligence data center in Vineland. The state Department of Environmental Protection discovered the generators during a July 29 inspection and said each unit had a capacity of 1,982 kilowatts. Reports from 6abc and The Sun Papers describe the penalty as the largest enforcement action against a data center in New Jersey. Together, the generators represent nearly 123 megawatts of potential power generation, making the case significant as AI facilities expand and demand large backup or temporary energy systems. DataOne has disputed the state’s findings but said it would apply for the required permits while moving towards a lower-emission fuel-cell system.The New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection inspected the DataOne site in Vineland on July 29. During the visit, officials found 62 stationary natural-gas generators installed and operating at the facility.The generators were not small household backup units. Each one had a rated capacity of 1,982 kilowatts, or nearly 2 megawatts.Together, the 62 engines represented approximately 122.9 megawatts of nameplate generation capacity, according to engineering industry publication ENR.State officials said DataOne had installed and operated the generators without first obtaining the preconstruction permits and valid operating certificates required under New Jersey’s Air Pollution Control Act.The generators had not been observed during a previous DEP inspection in December 2025. Their appearance at the site by July 2026 raised questions about when they were installed and how long they had operated before the inspection.The state’s enforcement action focused on the equipment itself, but the discovery also drew attention to the broader challenge of regulating rapidly expanding AI infrastructure. A large data center can require enormous amounts of dependable power, especially while a permanent electricity supply is being developed.New Jersey law requires stationary generators with a capacity of 37 kilowatts or more to obtain a preconstruction permit and a valid operating certificate. Each DataOne generator was rated at 1,982 kilowatts, making every unit substantially larger than the state’s permitting threshold.A preconstruction permit allows regulators to review a proposed source before it is installed. The review can consider expected emissions, fuel consumption, pollution controls, operating conditions and potential effects on nearby communities.An operating certificate confirms that the equipment can run under approved conditions. It also helps regulators monitor whether the source is complying with limits and reporting requirements.The permitting process is particularly important for combustion equipment. Natural-gas generators produce emissions such as nitrogen oxides and carbon monoxide, along with greenhouse gases. The amount released depends on the engines’ design, operating hours, fuel use and pollution-control systems.Without the required approvals, regulators may not have had complete information about the generators’ operation. Environmental groups said that made it difficult to determine how long the equipment had been running and what its overall impact might have been.The DEP issued an Administrative Order and Notice of Civil Penalty Assessment against DataOne. The order imposed a $1.07 million penalty and required the company to apply for the necessary permits or cease installing and operating the generators.Governor Mikie Sherrill’s administration described the fine as the largest enforcement action against a data center in New Jersey history.The penalty is also being presented as a warning to the wider technology industry. State officials said data centers must comply with air-quality laws even when they are being built quickly or using equipment described as temporary.Governor Sherrill said the state was taking action to ensure that the growth of data centers did not come at the expense of communities or the environment. DEP Commissioner Ed Potosnak said the action was intended to send a message that developers would be held accountable for pollution violations.The fine is large in dollar terms, although environmental advocates argued that a penalty of this size may not be enough to discourage billion-dollar infrastructure projects from moving ahead without approvals.DataOne has disputed the state’s interpretation of the generators’ status.The company said it disagreed with the determination that the equipment was operating in violation of the state’s permitting requirements. However, DataOne also said it would apply for the permits and continue discussions with the DEP.The company has described the generators as part of a temporary power arrangement. It said the facility was transitioning to fuel cells as its permanent power solution.DataOne’s position reflects the complex power needs of a large data center. A facility may require electricity before its permanent connection to the regional grid is complete. Developers can use on-site generators to provide power during construction, testing or early operations.But the state’s position is that temporary use does not remove the requirement to obtain permits. If the equipment is large enough to fall under the Air Pollution Control Act, its installation and operation must be reviewed by regulators.The DEP has ordered DataOne to obtain the approvals immediately or stop installing and operating the engines.DataOne’s Vineland facility is described as a 300-megawatt artificial intelligence data center. Its scale reflects the growing energy demand associated with AI computing.Artificial intelligence systems require powerful processors that operate in large clusters. These processors consume electricity and generate heat, requiring substantial cooling systems. Data centers also need backup power to prevent interruptions that could affect computing customers.The proposed 300-megawatt capacity is far larger than the electricity demand of an ordinary commercial building. The 62 generators discovered at the site represented almost 123 megawatts of generation capacity, showing how much power the facility needed even before the project reached its full planned scale.The rapid development of AI facilities has intensified debates about electricity supply, grid reliability, water use, emissions and local infrastructure. Communities may welcome construction activity and economic investment, but they also want assurances that large industrial operations will follow environmental rules.The Vineland case has brought those concerns into sharper focus because the facility’s power equipment was operating before the required approvals were in place.Residents living near the Vineland site had already raised concerns about noise from the generators.Large natural-gas engines produce a steady mechanical sound when running. When dozens of units operate in the same area, the combined noise can become difficult for nearby households to ignore, particularly at night.Local residents and environmental advocates have also questioned the possible effects on air quality. The concerns are not limited to emissions from one generator. They involve the combined output of 62 engines operating at a major industrial facility.The complaints have added a community dimension to the state’s enforcement action. For residents, the issue is not only whether DataOne eventually receives permits. They also want to know how the generators were installed, how long they operated without approvals and whether their use affected local living conditions.Noise and air pollution are regulated through separate rules, but both can influence how communities experience a large data center. A site can comply with one set of requirements while still attracting complaints about another aspect of its operation.Data centers depend on continuous electricity. Even a brief interruption can disrupt servers, cloud services and AI workloads.That demand can encourage developers to install on-site generation while they wait for permanent grid connections or other infrastructure. Natural-gas generators are widely used because they can produce electricity on demand and operate for long periods.However, large generator banks also create environmental obligations. Their operation may produce air pollutants, greenhouse gas emissions, noise and traffic linked to fuel or maintenance activities.The size of the DataOne installation made the permitting question especially important. Each engine was more than 50 times the state threshold requiring an air permit, according to NJ.com.The state’s enforcement action therefore concerns more than a technical paperwork issue. It involves whether a large source of potential pollution was placed into service without regulators having the opportunity to review it beforehand.DataOne said it planned to use low-emission fuel cells for the facility’s permanent power system.Fuel cells produce electricity through an electrochemical reaction rather than conventional combustion within an engine. Depending on the technology and fuel used, they can reduce local air pollutants and operate more quietly than a large collection of natural-gas generators.The company’s proposed transition could address some of the concerns surrounding the temporary engines. It may reduce noise, limit local emissions and provide a power source designed specifically for long-term data-center operations.However, the transition does not eliminate the immediate permitting issue. The generators are still operating or available for operation, and the DEP has required DataOne to obtain approvals or stop using them.The environmental benefits of fuel cells will also depend on their design, fuel source, efficiency and operating conditions. A lower-emission system may reduce local impacts, but it still requires oversight and compliance with applicable regulations.The Vineland penalty arrives as New Jersey and other states consider how to manage the rapid growth of data centers.Developers argue that AI and cloud computing facilities can bring jobs, construction spending, tax revenue and technology investment. State governments may also view data centers as part of a modern digital economy.At the same time, residents and environmental organisations have called for stricter review of their energy and environmental effects. They are asking regulators to examine emissions, noise, water consumption, electricity demand and the cost of connecting facilities to the power grid.The DataOne case may strengthen demands for closer oversight. Opponents of rapid development could point to the unpermitted generators as evidence that projects are moving faster than regulatory systems can handle.State officials, however, have presented the action as proof that existing laws can be enforced. The $1.07 million penalty and permit order show that large data centers are not exempt from air-pollution requirements, even when they are still under construction.DataOne must apply for and obtain the required permits or cease installing and operating the generators under the DEP order. The company has said it will work with state officials while continuing its transition to fuel cells.Further reviews may examine the engines’ operating history, emissions, noise and compliance with any conditions imposed through the permitting process.The case could also lead to closer inspections at other data centers using temporary or backup generators. Regulators may want developers to clarify their power plans before construction begins and determine whether temporary equipment requires approvals.For Vineland residents, the immediate question is whether the generators continue operating and whether the site’s noise and air-quality conditions change. For New Jersey officials, the larger question is how to support AI development without allowing environmental safeguards to become an afterthought.The record penalty makes the state’s position clear. Data centers may need enormous amounts of power, but their energy systems must still be permitted, monitored and operated within the law.
Article Summary: The new jersey department of environmental protection inspected the dataone site in vineland on july 29. During the visit, officials found 62 stationary natural-gas generators installed and operating at the facility. Each one had a rated capacity of 1,982 kilowatts, or nearly 2 megawatts.

Article Title: Millions of California households are getting electricity-bill credits automatically during the expensive summer months; the state says $886 million is being returned, averaging about $75 per househol
Article Text: Millions of California households received a sweet surprise in their electricity bills for the months of August and September. Under a new schedule designed to place relief in the hottest, highest-use months, homes received automatic credit. Governor Gavin Newsom's office said on Tuesday that customers of Pacific Gas and Electric, Southern California Edison and San Diego Gas & Electric will receive a combined $886 million in California Climate Credits this year, averaging about $75 per household across the three large utilities.Interestingly, the credits require no application. They appear automatically on eligible residential bills and are funded with proceeds from California’s Cap-and-Invest program, which requires large greenhouse-gas emitters to buy allowances. A portion of those proceeds is returned directly to utility customers rather than retained for other climate investments. The governor’s announcement distinguishes the $886 million going through the three largest electric utilities from the broader electric-credit program.The exact household amounts vary by provider. The California Public Utilities Commission’s 2026 schedule listed two credits of $36.18 for PG&E customers, two credits of $36 for Southern California Edison customers and two credits of $49.36 for SDG&E customers.Smaller utilities follow a separate schedule: Bear Valley, Liberty and Pacific Power customers receive their 2026 electric credits in April and November.The benefit is not a discount tied to a household’s income or consumption. Within each utility, eligible residential customers generally receive the same electric-credit amount, so its effect depends on the size of a customer’s bill. It also does not erase past-due balances or permanently lower a utility’s rates. Instead, it functions as a periodic return of allowance proceeds, visible as a credit line on the monthly statement.The CPUC previously distributed the major utilities’ electric credits in spring and fall. In an April decision announcing the change, the commission said moving them to August and September would better offset peak summer bills. The agency put total 2026 electric credits across investor-owned utilities and community choice aggregators at $894 million, alongside $520 million in natural-gas credits. Natural-gas customers continue to receive their 2026 credit in April; beginning in 2027, that credit moves to February to align with winter heating demand. The CPUC also directed utilities to improve bill labelling and customer outreach so recipients can identify the credit.The two statewide totals describe different scopes rather than competing calculations: the governor highlighted $886 million for customers of the three large electric utilities, while the CPUC’s $894 million figure includes the wider electric-credit system. The difference matters for customers served by smaller investor-owned utilities, whose credit months and amounts differ from the big-three schedule. Community choice customers may receive generation service from a local provider while the incumbent utility still delivers electricity and presents the credit on the bill.The CPUC said the revised schedule implements provisions of Assembly Bill 1207, enacted in 2025, and directs 5% of electric-utility allowance proceeds to a revolving fund for transmission projects. A later phase of the CPUC proceeding will consider further changes to the residential credit. For consumers, the immediate practical point is straightforward: eligible customers should see a line-item credit without enrolling, while the amount and month depend on the utility serving their home.

Article Title: Anthropic’s Claude AI discovers new enzyme system in bacteria-infecting viruses; Dario Amodei says: We believe AI for biology is on a similar...
Article Text:
Claude spotted a CRISPR-like pattern that earlier studies missed

Around 950 Claude agents searched DNA data for 21 hours

CRISPR pioneer Feng Zhang calls the finding worth a closer look

Dario Amodei says AI in biology is on the same curve as maths

Anthropic says its Claude AI has found a previously unknown enzyme system inside viruses that infect bacteria, and its layout looks a lot like CRISPR, the natural machinery behind the world's best-known gene editing tool. The company has named it array-associated reverse transcriptase, or ART, and says Claude did most of the work after its scientists gave it a single broad prompt.The finding is the first result from Anthropic's new life sciences research group and wet lab, set up in the Bay Area this spring. What ART does is still unknown. CEO Dario Amodei said as much in a post on X, noting that its precise function, biotech usefulness "(if any)" and significance are not yet clear. "But at minimum it is work I would have been proud to do as a PhD student," he wrote.ART has three parts. There is a reverse transcriptase (RT), an enzyme that copies RNA into DNA. There is a partner gene of unknown function sitting beside it. And there is a long array of evenly spaced DNA repeats.That repeat array is what invites the CRISPR comparison. In CRISPR systems, a similar array stores a bank of RNA sequences, which is what makes them programmable.The RT itself, found in a jumbo phage, had been identified in earlier research. Anthropic says Claude appears to be the first to notice the array and the accessory protein around it. Early lab tests show the array is expressed as a set of distinct short RNAs, which suggests ART may work in a way similar to CRISPR. Experiments to confirm its function are ongoing, and a pre-print is already out.Anthropic says roughly 950 Claude agents spent 21 hours combing through a massive database of DNA sequences, using 210 million tokens along the way. They gathered more than 200,000 RTs, shortlisted 3,500 new candidate systems and narrowed those to 20, each with a report written for human review. The company says this kind of analysis can take an expert scientist weeks to months.The moment of discovery came while one agent was reading raw DNA next to an odd-looking RT. Its note read: "that's a CRISPR-like … repeat array?!" It then counted the repeats, measured their spacing, compared the layout with known RT systems and checked the literature before flagging it.Amodei described the split carefully. The work was done "mostly, though not entirely, by Claude," he wrote. The team picked the research area, Claude read the literature and genome data and proposed experiments, and human scientists ran them. The lab only handles biosafety level 1 and 2 work, with no pathogens that infect people, and the team used Claude Science and Claude Code, the same tools any scientist can access.Feng Zhang, one of the pioneers of CRISPR genome editing and a professor at MIT and the Broad Institute, reviewed the pre-print. He called it "an exciting example of how AI agents can contribute to biological discovery" and said the RNA-repeat arrays were "intriguing and merits further investigation."Amodei also pointed out that a Stanford team, working separately, recently described a different RT system with a similar array. The two evolved independently, he said.Amodei used the announcement to make a wider case. In 2023, he wrote, AI models struggled with high-school maths. By late 2026, they are beginning to solve some of the hardest open problems in the field. He believes biology is on a similar exponential trend.Biology, of course, needs lab work. Amodei says humans working with AI can validate key results in a few weeks, and that Claude may one day run lab equipment itself with safeguards in place, though Anthropic isn't doing that yet.He was clear that faster discovery won't shorten clinical trials. It could, however, send many more promising drug candidates into the pipeline. That links back to his 2024 essay Machines of Loving Grace, where he wrote that AI could help "cure most diseases in 5-10 years."Anthropic now plans to expand its life sciences team and is inviting outside scientists to pitch collaborations. Whether ART ever becomes a tool on the scale of CRISPR is anyone's guess. What Anthropic has shown is that Claude can find something in public DNA data that had been sitting there, unnoticed, until now.
Article Summary: Claude spotted a crispr-like pattern that earlier studies missed.around 950 claude agents searched dna data for 21 hours.crispr pioneer feng zhang calls the finding worth a closer look.dario amodei says ai in biology is on the same curve as maths. Anthropic plans to expand its life sciences team and is inviting outside scientists to pitch collaborations.

Article Title: Apple Siri settlement: iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 16 owners can now claim up to $95; here's how to file
Article Text:
Only US buyers of seven iPhone models qualify for the payout

Filing an Apple Siri settlement claim needs your iPhone serial number

Claims close on December 21, but payments will wait until 2027

Apple has opened the claims window for its $250 million (about Rs 2,200 crore) settlement over the delayed Apple Intelligence upgrade to Siri. Eligible iPhone owners in the US can now file for a payout of $25 per device. That figure could rise to $95, depending on how many people come forward.The class action, Landsheft et al. v. Apple Inc., accused the company of selling the iPhone 16 as "built for Apple Intelligence" while the smarter Siri shown at WWDC 2024 was nowhere near ready. That upgraded Siri only reached users with iOS 27 earlier this month, more than two years after its first demo. Apple has denied any wrongdoing, and the settlement terms say it is not an admission of liability.The claim covers purchases made between June 10, 2024, and March 29, 2025. The iPhone 15 Pro and 15 Pro Max qualify, along with the entire iPhone 16 lineup: the iPhone 16, 16 Plus, 16 Pro, 16 Pro Max and the budget iPhone 16e.You must be the original buyer, and the phone must have been bought for personal or work use, not resale. Indian buyers of the same models are not covered, since the case was filed and settled in the US.Claims are filed on the official website, SmartphoneAISettlement.com.The form asks for your name, address, phone number and the iPhone's serial number, which you'll find under Settings > General > About. If you don't have the serial number, the form will take your Apple Account email and the phone number linked to the device instead.Eligible owners should also receive an email over the coming days with a claim ID and PIN. You can still file without them. Each device needs its own claim, and only one payment is allowed per phone.The $95 maximum depends on how many iPhone owners filePayouts start at $25 per device and can climb to $95 if fewer valid claims come in than expected. Payment options include PayPal, Venmo, direct deposit and a paper check.Ryan Clarkson, co-lead counsel on the case and founder of Clarkson Law Firm, described the fund as the largest false advertising settlement on record.The deadline to file is December 21, 2026. A federal district court in San Jose will hold the final approval hearing on February 24, 2027, and payments will only go out after that. Any appeal could delay them further.Anyone unsure about eligibility can call the settlement administrator on 1-888-988-8945. For those who bought an iPhone 16 waiting for the new Siri, the money will arrive even later than the feature did.
Article Summary: Apple has opened the claims window for its $250 million settlement over the siri upgrade. Eligible iphone owners in the us can now file for a payout of $25 per device. That figure could rise to $95, depending on how many people come forward. Only us buyers of seven iphone models qualify for the payout.

Article Title: TRAI orders Airtel, Jio, Vodafone Idea to launch voice, SMS-only plans for every validity period
Article Text:
Why TRAI is pushing for voice and SMS-only plans

Telcos pushed back and lost

What this means for users

India’s telecom regulator TRAI has directed the major telecom operations — Airtel, Reliance Jio and Vodafone Idea to roll out affordable recharge plans offering only voice and SMS services starting October 21, 2026. As reported by the Times of India, this move from the regulator is aimed at low-income users who do not require bundled data services but need flexible, short-term options for calls and messaging. TRAI’s order mandates that telcos provide shorter validity Special Tariff Vouchers (STVs) for voice and SMS, with durations of up to 30 days. Importantly, these plans must allow monthly renewal on the same date each month, defaulting to the last day if the exact date is unavailable. In addition, operators must also offer at least one longer validity voice-SMS plan to match existing bundled offerings.This isn't TRAI's first attempt at solving this problem. The regulator had already mandated in December 2024 that every telecom operator offer at least one voice-and-SMS-only STV. But TRAI found that outcome insufficient — operators offered only a handful of such plans, often with limited validity options, and crucially, priced them relatively high without reducing costs proportionally to the data being removed.This latest amendment is designed to close that gap by requiring parity across every validity period rather than just one token offering.The regulator's broader reasoning is straightforward: many users — particularly senior citizens, feature-phone users, people who rely on Wi-Fi or a second device for data, and those with second SIMs — don't need mobile data bundled into every recharge, and shouldn't be forced to pay for data they'll never use just to get calling and texting.Jio, Airtel, and Vodafone Idea had all formally opposed the mandate during TRAI's consultation process, calling it anti-consumer, technically impractical, and inconsistent with the regulator's own policy of tariff forbearance. Jio specifically argued that standalone voice plans are technically incompatible with how modern 4G and 5G networks operate, since voice functions as an application running over an underlying data network on IP-based infrastructure. The company also warned that cheap, short-validity voice-only plans could lower the barrier for scammers, potentially fueling more unsolicited commercial communication and cyber fraud. Jio added that 88% of its entry-level subscribers already actively use data, and that existing voice-only plans have historically seen limited uptake.Vodafone Idea raised a separate concern, warning that stripping data out of plans could expose users to unexpected charges elsewhere. Despite these objections, TRAI proceeded with the mandate, evidently unconvinced that the operators' concerns outweighed the consumer protection rationale behind the rule.Once implemented, the change should give consumers meaningfully more flexibility than before. Users who mainly rely on calling and texting — or who access the internet through Wi-Fi or a separate device — will be able to pick a voice-and-SMS-only plan matching virtually any validity period they'd normally choose for a data-inclusive plan, at a proportionally lower price. It's also expected to be a practical win for dual-SIM users, who can now dedicate one SIM purely to calls and SMS at a lower cost rather than paying for a redundant data allowance they don't need on that connection.Whether operators price these new mandatory plans generously or find workarounds to limit their appeal, as some consumer advocates have suggested happened after the 2024 mandate, remains to be seen once the October 21 deadline arrives.
Article Summary: India’s telecom regulator trai has directed the major telecom operations to roll out affordable recharge plans offering only voice and sms services starting october 21, 2026. The move is aimed at low-income users who do not require bundled data services but need flexible, short-term options for calls and messaging.

Article Title: How to find your lost Android phone using Google Find Hub
Article Text:
Representative Image

Set up Find Hub on your Android phone before you lose it

Location and Bluetooth are turned on

"Allow device to be located" is enabled under the Find Hub settings (look under Security, or Google > All Services > Personal & Device Safety)

Offline finding is set to "With network in busy places only" or "With network everywhere"

A PIN, pattern or password is set, since offline finding won't work without one

You're signed in to a Google account you can still access

How to locate a lost Android phone on a map

Mark as lost: Locks the phone with your PIN and shows a message and contact number on the lock screen. On phones running Android 17 with fingerprint or Face Unlock, it adds two-step verification too. Keep the message short, as scammers can use those details to trick you into unlocking the phone for them.

Remote Lock: No Google password handy? You can lock the screen using just your phone number.

Factory reset: Your last resort. It permanently deletes everything and removes the phone from Find Hub, so you can't track it after that.

Lost your Android phone? Google's Find Hub is the first place to check, and you don't need a second Android device to use it. Any web browser, on a laptop or a friend's iPhone, can show you where your phone was last seen, make it ring, lock it, or wipe it clean.Find Hub is the new name for Google's Find My Device. It runs on an opt-in network of millions of Android devices that pick up Bluetooth signals from lost phones, earbuds and tracker tags, then quietly report their location back to the owner. That location data is end-to-end encrypted, so only you can see it. Google says it can't either.Find Hub switches on automatically once you sign in with a Google account. But a few settings decide how useful it will be on the day your phone goes missing. Check these now:Newer Pixel phones can even be located several hours after they've been switched off. Menu names vary a little by brand, but the options look similar on most Android phones.Open the Find Hub app on another Android phone or a Wear OS watch, or visit the Find Hub website on any browser. Sign in with the same Google account and pick your phone from the device list. The map shows its last known location, and you can get directions through Google Maps.If the phone is somewhere nearby, tap Play sound. It rings at full volume for five minutes, even on silent. Within 10 metres, the Find Nearby feature shows a shape that fills in as you get closer.Lock or erase your Android phone if it's stolenIf the phone is gone for good, act fast.Check those settings once, and the next time your phone goes missing, you'll know exactly where to look.
Article Summary: Find hub is the new name for google's find my device. It runs on an opt-in network of millions of android devices that pick up bluetooth signals from lost phones, earbuds and tracker tags. Any web browser, on a laptop or a friend's iphone can show you where your phone was last seen, make it ring, lock it, or wipe it clean.

Article Title: Meta unveils camera-free Ray-Ban Audio glasses and a keychain AI companion at Connect 2026
Article Text:
Ray-Ban Meta Audio : cameras out, all-day wearability in

Muse Charm: an AI agent you can put on a keychain

At its annual Meta Connect event, Facebook-parent Meta has announced a major expansion of its consumer hardware portfolio with the launch of new Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses and a quirky Muse AI keychain. The new products unveiled highlight Meta’s AI push to embed AI agents into everyday life simply by blending fashion, utility and entertainment. The new Ray-Ban Meta glasses lineup builds on Meta’s partnership with EssilorLuxottica. The glasses now feature deeper AI integration, including voice-controlled access to Meta’s AI assistant, improved audio quality, and enhanced camera capabilities. On the other hand, Meta Muse AI keychain is a pocket-sized device described as “Tamagotchi-like.” The gadget acts as a portable AI agent, offering playful interactions, reminders, and personalized assistance. Meta positioned Muse as a way to make AI more approachable, turning everyday tasks into engaging experiences.The headline hardware announcement was Ray-Ban Meta Audio, Meta's first-ever camera-free smart glasses, developed through its ongoing partnership with EssilorLuxottica. By ditching the camera setup entirely, Meta managed to bring the glasses down to just 43 grams — noticeably lighter than the roughly 50g standard Ray-Ban Meta models and far lighter than the 70g Display glasses — while still packing in hands-free music and podcast playback, calling, and conversations with Meta's AI assistant.The glasses come in Clubmaster and Burbank styles, with customizable temple tips, nose pads, and overextension hinges for a more tailored fit, and support a wide range of optical prescriptions.Battery life is rated at up to 12 hours on a single charge, extendable to roughly 48 additional hours using the included charging case. Ray-Ban Meta Audio launches October 13 at $349, with pre-orders open now.Meta also used the moment to introduce Hearing Enhancement, an FDA-cleared accessibility feature arriving later this year for supported AI glasses. Using the glasses' six-speaker array, the feature is designed to help people who are hard of hearing pick out speech more clearly in noisy environments, letting users adjust left-right audio balance or shift to mono audio in one ear. Meta is pricing it at $149.99 as a one-time purchase, or bundling it into a Meta One subscription, framing it as a notably more affordable alternative to traditional hearing aids, which the company says typically start around $800. A 30-day free trial will also be available.Beyond the audio-only model, Meta also refreshed its standard Ray-Ban Meta line with the Gen 3 glasses, adding a slimmer build, longer battery life, a 12MP camera, and 3K Ultra HD video recording. The company additionally previewed a new hologram calling feature for Ray-Ban Meta Display users, letting someone do a quick self-capture with their phone to generate a hologram visible to whoever they're calling — expected to arrive in early access on WhatsApp in the US within the next few months.The event's true "one more thing" moment came when CEO Mark Zuckerberg unveiled Muse Charm, a small, palm-sized wearable designed to give people another physical way to interact with Muse, Meta's recently launched and increasingly popular personal AI agent.The device houses a tiny screen displaying Jolly, the cute animated avatar Meta has built to represent Muse, and is meant to be carried in a pocket or clipped onto a keychain. Zuckerberg explained that the team condensed the entire Muse experience — including its real-time voice and avatar system — into a device small enough to live on a keychain while remaining constantly available to talk to. A fingerprint sensor built into the corner of the device lets users start a conversation instantly, without needing to unlock a phone or open an app first. For anyone not wearing AI glasses, Zuckerberg positioned Muse Charm as the fastest possible way to talk to Muse and show it what's happening around you.The gadget leans into a distinctly Tamagotchi-like aesthetic — small, personality-driven, and designed to keep users continually engaged with Meta's AI software. Zuckerberg acknowledged the hardware isn't quite ready for release, saying the team still needs to finalize how its internal components are laid out, but confirmed Muse Charm is on track to ship in time for the December holiday season.
Article Summary: Muse charm is a pocket-sized device that acts as a portable ai agent. Ray-ban meta audio is meta's first-ever camera-free smart glasses. The company also introduced hearing enhancement, an fda-cleared accessibility feature. Zuckerberg acknowledged the hardware isn't quite ready for release.

Our idea of ‘Intelligent Ears’ is simple: earbuds that can listen, understand, converse and assist. But this is just the beginning, we are working on multiple other use cases. For ten years, Boat has helped India listen. Now, we want to help India listen, understand, converse and assist”.The Boat Airdopes Prime 800 D combines Crest AI capabilities with Dolby Audio and 11mm dynamic drivers tuned to Boat Signature Sound. The earbuds offer up to 45 hours of total playback, Multipoint Connectivity and four microphones with AI-ENx technology, bringing together entertainment, communication and intelligent assistance in one device.Crest AI is also available on the Boat Airdopes Prime 701 ANC and Boat Nirvana Ion ANC. The Boat Airdopes Prime 800 D, Boat Airdopes Prime 701 ANC and Boat Nirvana Ion ANC are available through the Boat website and leading e-commerce platforms.
Article Summary: Boat launches smart earbuds range with crest ai platform built with google gemini. The lineup includes boat airdopes prime 800 and boat nirvana ion anc. With the launch, boat is introducing a new proposition for personal audio — ‘intelligent ears’

Article Title: Motorola showcases Signature 27 with 50MP main camera and 200MP periscope telephoto camera
Article Text:
Motorola launches Signature 27 with 50MP main camera and 200MP periscope telephoto camera

Motorola Signature 27 features

Motorola Signature 27 operating system

Motorola has showcased the Signature 27, its second smartphone in the Signature series and one of the first phones announced with Qualcomm’s latest Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 chipset. The smartphone was unveiled at the Snapdragon Summit 2026 on Tuesday and comes with a 50MP Sony LYTIA 910 main camera and a 200MP periscope telephoto camera. Motorola is also changing its naming system with this phone, using the final two digits of the upcoming year for its new generations. The company has not yet announced the price or exact sale date, but says the Signature 27 will launch globally later this year.The Motorola Signature 27 is powered by Qualcomm’s new Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 processor. Motorola says the chipset brings improvements to on-device AI, camera performance, gaming response and download speeds. The phone also comes with Motorola’s ArcticMesh cooling system. It combines diamond-infused thermal gel, liquid metal and copper mesh with a redesigned 3D vapour chamber. Motorola says the new vapour chamber is 40% larger than the previous generation.Motorola Signature 27 gets a 50MP Sony LYTIA 910 main camera along with a 200MP periscope telephoto camera.Motorola has also introduced its Video Enhancement Engine, which uses AI to study a scene before and during video recording and adjust colour tones in real time.The phone will also support Google's Gemini Omni, which can use prompts, photos or existing video clips to create a finished video. Google's Lyria can be used to generate music and soundtracks.The phone will be available in Pantone Coal Smoke and Pantone Capulet Green. The Coal Smoke version has a woven texture designed to improve grip and durability, while Capulet Green gets a brushed, textile-inspired finish.Motorola says the Signature 27 will receive seven years of OS upgrades and is expected to launch with Android 17. It is also the company's first smartphone with Audio by B&O, with the branding etched onto the rear panel.Motorola has not yet revealed the phone's display, battery capacity, charging speed, RAM, storage or other camera sensors. Pricing and the exact launch date are also yet to be announced.

Article Title: AI malware is becoming its own category: Researchers found a malicious program that uses multiple AI models to decide what to do
Article Text:
AI malware is becoming its own category: Researchers found a malicious program that uses multiple AI models to decide what to do

How does the AI-powered malware work

Researchers are finding more AI-powered malware

What the findings suggest

Researchers have reportedly found a malicious program that uses AI model to help decide what it should do next. The malware, called CLOSEDQUORUM, can contact up to four AI models, including DeepSeek, Qwen, Mistral and Google Gemini. Instead of relying only on instructions written by its developers, the program asks these AI systems for guidance and uses their responses to decide its next steps. Reported by Wired, the discovery was made by researchers at Cisco Talos, who have also created an open-source framework to track malware that uses AI.CLOSEDQUORUM is designed for Windows and can use several AI services at the same time. Researchers describe the setup as a kind of “hive mind”, because the malware can seek decisions from multiple AI models. If one AI service is unavailable, the others can continue working.As stated in the report, researchers also found no mechanism that would allow a human to step in and control the process.The malware is designed to steal login credentials and cryptocurrency. Researchers also found links to cybercrime forums discussing credit-card fraud dating back to 2025. However, they could not confirm who created CLOSEDQUORUM or whether it has been used in real-world attacks.Cisco Talos created the Cognitive Artifact Intelligence Research Network (CAIRN) after researchers began finding signs that attackers were integrating AI into malware.Ryan Fetterman of Cisco Talos said AI integration leaves behind identifiable “fingerprints” that can help researchers track and classify these programs.“The core idea is that AI integration has these vestiges, like fingerprints, that are left behind... That gives us a signal that we can use to track these samples, classify them, and look at what's happening,” Fetterman said.When Fetterman first searched for AI-integrated malware, he found only around nine named malware families, along with several proof-of-concept examples. After CAIRN was developed, researchers identified about 20 additional examples within a few months.The findings suggest that AI is becoming more deeply integrated into some malware rather than simply being used by hackers to write code or create phishing messages. Matt Olney of Cisco Talos said attackers are now beginning to operationalise AI.“Initially, everyone saw AI as a productivity tool, right?... Now what we're seeing is that it's becoming operationalized.”He said AI could allow attackers to run more campaigns, target more systems and handle different computers because the technology can provide responses and guidance in the background.
Article Summary: Malware can contact up to four ai models, including deepseek, qwen, mistral and google gemini. Researchers describe the setup as a kind of ‘hive mind’ because the malware can seek decisions from multiple ai models. If one ai service is unavailable, the others can continue working.

Article Title: Netflix unveils ‘VOID’, an AI model that can change a movie plot
Article Text:
Netflix

How Netflix VOID works



Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background. VOID goes a step further: after erasing an object from a scene, it calculates how the surrounding environment should realistically respond to its absence, and in the process it adjusts the behaviour of other elements in the frame accordingly.The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness that sets it apart from several existing tools.For example, imagine this scenario: A movie director has just wrapped up a multi-million dollar action sequence where the star drives straight into a fiery, head-on collision. The cars explode, debris scatters, and the scene is a wrap.But suddenly, there is request to change the scene: The character survives and drive off into the sunset instead. This would mean costly reshoots or millions spent on computer-generated graphics.Netflix’s VOID can alter the scene and digitally erase the collision, the second vehicle, the smoke, and the flying debris. It will then generate new, realistic footage of pristine pavement, making it look as though the main character simply drove down an empty, peaceful road.The AI’s ‘magic’ lies in its grasp of real-world physics. Let us understand this by a different example. If a video shows a person jumping into a pool and splashing water onto the deck, VOID can completely erase the person. It will then intelligently alter the water and the wet concrete, leaving behind a perfectly still, undisturbed pool as if nobody had ever jumped in.“To train the model, we generate a new paired dataset of counterfactual object removals using Kubric and HUMOTO, where removing an object requires altering downstream physical interactions. During inference, a vision-language model identifies regions of the scene affected by the removed object. These regions are then used to guide a video diffusion model that generates physically consistent counterfactual outcomes,” Netflix said.“Experiments on both synthetic and real data show that our approach better preserves consistent scene dynamics after object removal compared to prior video object removal methods,” the company added.Netflix isn’t keeping this powerful tool locked behind studio doors, and made the VOID model available to the public on the AI platform Hugging Face, allowing anyone to download and use it.While there are already several video-altering tools on the market, such as Runway, DiffuEraser, and ProPainter, the Netflix team claims VOID is vastly superior, as per The Register.
Article Summary: Netflix has unveiled an ai model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background.

Article Title: AI data centers are causing 'stress' not just to tech companies, but also private insurers
Article Text:
Massive investments, growing risks



Unique challenges for data centre insurance companies

AI data centers are reportedly putting new pressure on the insurance industry. According to a CNBC report, experts warn that the rapid growth of these projects is becoming a “stress test” not just for tech companies, but also for private insurers and lenders. Consulting firm McKinsey estimates that global spending on data centers could reach $7 trillion by 2030. As costs rise, tech giants are increasingly relying on private equity, private credit and debt to fund these projects. The scale of investments is creating challenges for insurers.“When you put $10 to $20 billion plus in a single location, it creates capacity issues in the marketplace,” said Tom Harper, data center leader at insurance broker Gallagher as quoted in the CNBC report.He added that the sector has been a “real stress test” over the last few years, as insurers struggle to provide coverage for such large and complex projects. While these facilities are seen as high-quality assets, Harper said insuring them has become difficult due to their size and risk concentration.Private data center deals have crossed $10 billion regularly, with some reaching as high as $40 billion. Companies including Nvidia, Microsoft and BlackRock have already taken part in large investment deals.Rajat Rana, partner at Quinn Emanuel Urquhart & Sullivan, described the scale as unprecedented. “We’re talking about trillions of dollars, and almost going back to the same cycle where there’s almost no transparency about the financing structures — the scale is astronomical,” he said. He added that the boom in AI data centers could be “the largest peacetime investment project in human history.”Experts say the way these projects are financed is adding another layer of risk. Much of the funding is happening through complex and less transparent debt structures. Rana warned that this trend feels like “deja vu,” referring to past financial cycles. He said the lack of transparency could create risks for investors, insurers and pension funds.As stated in the CNBC report, data centers offer unique challenges due to their mix of real estate and advanced technology. Insurers are now designing custom policies to manage these risks. However, challenges remain. Large facilities are often located in areas prone to extreme weather, and they store expensive equipment, sometimes even before installation.Another key concern is the mismatch between the lifespan of data centers and the hardware they use. While data centers can last decades, GPUs — the chips powering AI — typically last around seven years. Rana described this as a “GPU debt treadmill,” saying, “This is almost like a treadmill that these AI data centers are running on.”He explained that companies may need to keep raising debt to upgrade infrastructure as technology evolves.
Article Summary: Private data center deals have crossed $10 billion regularly, with some reaching as high as $40 billion. Mckinsey estimates that global spending on data centers could reach $7 trillion by 2030. Tech giants are increasingly relying on private equity, private credit and debt to fund these projects.
